blocks.text: Remediation Jobs runs a script on selected devices as a job, and you can schedule the job as needed. Scripts are useful for remediating software issues by running PowerShell scripts on the selected devices. The Jobs page gathers parameter support and script output to categorize each job into the In Progress, Completed, or Scheduled tables for easy visibility and management. If a script fails, you can re-run the job or edit the script as required to run the job again.
Prior to running scripts on a device, you must have:

blocks.item: The appropriate subscription level to support Remediation. To learn more, see Ranges & Limitations.
The appropriate permission level to configure scripts. To learn more, see Adding ZDX Roles.
The device must have:
The minimum required versions of Zscaler Client Connector and ZDX Module
The supported OS
To learn more, see Supported Versions & Feature Compatibility.

blocks.text: From the navigation menu, go to Digital Experience > Devices > Jobs. To manage the number of jobs on the Jobs page, you can:

blocks.item: Start a new job.
Click Start New Job.
The Start Remediation Job window appears.
See image.
Enter a Name for the job.
Under Select Script:
Script: Search and select which script you want to run for the job. You can also create a script.
Script Details: If you configured script parameters or an end user notification, then you can modify the script parameters and preview the end user notification.
Script Run Settings: Enter the number of seconds the script runs for the job.
Under Select Devices, click Add to open the Select Devices drawer.
Criteria: Select Devices, Users, User Groups, Locations, Location Groups, or Departments.
Display selected only: Enable to display only the selected items.
Search: You can search for the name of the selected criteria. Click the Remove icon to reset your search.
Click Done to save your selection.
You cannot select a device if it does not meet the version compatibility or OS. To learn more, see Supported Versions & Feature Compatibility.
See image.
Under Job Details:
Wait for devices to be online for a maximum of: Enter the number of minutes, hours, or days a script must wait to run on a device.
Schedule Job for later: Enable to select a date on which to run the script.
Click Save. If you enable Schedule Job for later, click Schedule.
Edit a job.
You can edit a job on the page if it's Scheduled.
Click the Edit icon on the job that you want to modify.
In the Edit Remediation Job window, modify the fields as needed.
See image.
Click Schedule.
Delete a job.
You can delete to cancel or abort a job on any table.
Click the Delete icon.
In the Delete Remediation Job window, click Delete.

blocks.text: There are three Jobs tables based on the status of the job: In Progress, Completed, and Scheduled. These tables help you focus on which jobs need attention by providing granular details of the success rate or progress of each job.
For each table on the Jobs page (Digital Experience > Devices > Jobs), you can:

blocks.item: View the In Progress, Completed, or Scheduled tables based on the job's progress.
Click View Scripts to view a collection of configured or predefined scripts on the Scripts page.
Start a new job.
Search for jobs in the respective table.
Modify the columns displayed in the table.
Modify the number of jobs to display per page.
Navigate through pages of jobs.

blocks.text: Each job has a status at any point of time and can be one of the following:

table: The job is currently running the remote script on selected devices.
The job is scheduled to run a remote script on selected devices.
The job was stopped while running a remote script. Jobs are capable of being stopped or aborted if the job has not entered its ending phase.
The job has successfully completed running the remote script on all selected devices.

blocks.text: The In Progress table provides the following:

blocks.item: A list of jobs that are in progress to view the following information:
Name: The name of the job. Click the Name to view job details.
Progress: A progression bar to display the percentage of job completion.
Script: The name of the script.
Operating System: The OS the script is for.
Devices: The number of devices selected for the job.
Created By: The user that started the job.
Started On: The timestamp of when the job started.
Actions: The available actions for the job.
View the job details.
Stop the job.

blocks.text: The Completed table provides the following:

blocks.item: A list of jobs that are completed to view the following information:
Name: The name of the job. The status of the job is displayed if the script run has Expired or Aborted. Click the Name to view job details.
Success Rate: A percentage display bar to indicate how many of the jobs were completed over the number of selected devices.
Script: The name of the script.
Operating System: The OS the script is for.
Devices: The number of devices selected for the job.
Created By: The user that started the job.
Started On: The timestamp of when the job started.
Ended On: The timestamp of when the job ended.
Actions: The available actions for the job.
View the job details where you can view the impacted devices, select and export a list of the impacted devices, or view the script output.
Rerun the job.
Delete the job.

blocks.text: The Scheduled table provides the following:

blocks.item: A list of jobs that are completed to view the following information:
Name: The name of the job. Click the Name to view job details.
Script: The name of the script.
Operating System: The OS the script is for.
Devices: The number of devices selected for the job.
Created By: The user that started the job.
Scheduled for: The timestamp of when the job is scheduled to start.
Actions: The available actions for the job.
Edit the job.
Delete the job.

blocks.text: You can view a job's granular details by clicking a row on any of the tables. Each job includes:

blocks.item: Under Job Details:
Success Rate: The percentage bar to indicate how many times the job was completed.
Success: The number of devices that have completed the job.
Failed: The number of devices that have failed to run the script.
If the job is aborted, then Digital Experience (ZDX) tries its best effort to stop the script.
Script: The name of the script.
Operating System: The OS the script is for.
Devices: The number of selected devices.
Created By: The user that started the job.
Started On: The timestamp of when the job started.
Ended On: The timestamp of when the job ended.
Targeted: The number of devices, users, user groups, locations, location groups, or departments that are targeted for the job. The targeted number is based on the job's selection.

Under the Devices table, you can view each group of devices based on their job status (All, Success, or Failed). All is the default view of both Success and Failed jobs on selected devices. Each row has:
Device: The name of the device.
User: The name of the user.
Execution Status: The status of the job.
Error Message: A descriptive error message as to why the job failed.
Result: The result of the job.
Script Output: The script output when the job is completed successfully. You can click the View icon to view the entire script output or request logs.
Last Updated On: The timestamp of when the script was last updated to run on the device.

blocks.text: If the job failed to run the script on a device, you can view where the remote script did not run on inactive or unavailable devices by clicking View Devices Where Script Did Not Run. Click Rerun Job to run the job as a new job with prefilled criteria.
Consider the following when configuring scripts:

blocks.item: You can configure only up to the maximum number of scripts based on your subscription. To learn more, see Ranges & Limitations.
You cannot select a device if it does not meet the version compatibility or OS. To learn more, see Supported Versions & Feature Compatibility.

When the user accepts a job and the script does not run due to an expired certificate or an invalid certificate, then you must upload the script again with a valid script certificate. To learn more, see Preparing Custom Script Signing.
